newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Naphtha/Mogas - Rayong sells prompt mogas.
newsitem.headline: Asia Naphtha/Mogas - Rayong sells prompt mogas.

text.p: Light distillate prices held steady on Friday amid a lack of firm direction, traders said.
Gasoline was dull with traders waiting for the results of a Thai tender which closed late on Friday.

Thai refiner Rayong Refinery Co Ltd awarded its tender to sell 180,000-barrels of 92-octane unleaded gasoline to Shell Singapore at 70 cents per barrel below Singapore quotes on a free-on-board basis, industry sources said.
The tender was for the cargo to be lifted June 23-27 from Map Ta Phut on the eastern seaboard.
The 145,000 barrel-per-day (bpd) refinery is a joint venture between the Royal Dutch Shell Group and the Petroleum Authority of Thailand (PTT).
The Rayong refinery just restarted its 30,000 bpd reformer on Thursday June 19 after a 10-day maintenance shutdown, sources close to the company said.
European major offered 92-octane fob Singapore at $23.35 per barrel, down from $23.70 on Thursday.
Some traders said although the offer for the grade had weakened, 95-octane should hold steady at a 90 cent differential.
"The 92-octane is just being artificially supported by selling into Indonesia," a trader said.
Indonesia is expected to buy around 500,000 barrels per month in July and August on the back of refinery turnarounds.
Naphtha traders were preparing for the forward open-specification contract meeting in Tokyo next week.
The weak prompt market kept naphtha prices in contango with July swaps talked at $20.35/$20.55 per barrel and August at $20.55/$20.65.
But September was talked on par with August as fundamentals are expectred to improve then, when petrochemical plants return from turnarounds.
Taiwan's state-owned Chinese Petroleum Corp (CPC) issued a tender to buy 28,000-tonnes of August naphthenic and aromatic (N+A) naphtha, a company official said.
CPC requires the cargo for August 1-31 delivery on a cost-and-freight (c+f) basis to Kaohsiung.
The tender closes June 25 and is valid for two days.
CPC's last tender, for July 20-31 delivery, was awarded at slightly above $215 per tonne c+f Kaohsiung.
But on the supply side, India is expected to export its normal five to six cargoes in July.
State-owned Indian Oil Corp (IOC) is expected to award its tenders for the first two July cargoes - HAN from Cochin and and Bombay, later on Friday.
IOC issued its third July tender, offering 27,000 tonnes of LAN lifting from Madras July 6-8, a source close to IOC said.
The tender offering the cargo from the east coast, closes June 25 and is valid until June 26.
IOC's last Madras LAN cargo, lifting in June, was awarded at $22 per tonne below Japanese spot quotes on a free-on-board basis to a South Korean refiner, sources said.
